stories.title: At least 552 dead and 1,400 missing after Nepal-Tibet floods
stories.summary: Rescuers have reached previously inaccessible areas as Nepal appeals for international aid and continues to attempt to rescue 100 workers trapped in a hydropower plant tunnel. More than 1,400 people are missing and at least 552 have been killed after devastating floods tore through the border region between Nepal and Tibet, as rescuers reached some of the worst-hit areas for the first time. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said on Friday that early estimates suggested about 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday's disaster and warned that the death toll was expected to rise. "The trauma of this event is enormous," said David Fisher, the IFRC's head of delegation for Nepal. He said washed-out roads and bridges, along with disrupted mobile phone coverage and electricity supplies, meant rescuers had still been unable to reach some of the hardest-hit areas. Nepalese police put the country's death toll at least 547 on Friday, while Chinese state media has confirmed five deaths on the Tibetan side of the border. Professional rescue teams have now reached the main disaster zone in Tibet. China's Xinhua news agency said teams from Tibet and neighbouring Sichuan arrived at the "core rescue site" on Friday afternoon. Chinese state media also said 499 residents and 555 tourists had been evacuated from the disaster zone. The nationalities of the tourists were not immediately disclosed. In Nepal, the military said it had located people trapped around the Trishuli 3A hydropower project and was working to bring them to safety. More than 100 people remained trapped in the area, while around 350 workers and residents had already been rescued, army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet said.

stories.title: Japan's controversial WWII heroes: How one kamikaze pilot escaped certain death
stories.summary: Towards the end of World War II, as US troops advanced across the Pacific, Japan resorted to a desperate strategy: kamikaze attacks. Thousands of Japanese pilots, with an average age of just 21, were ordered to crash their explosive-laden planes into enemy ships. More than 3,800 pilots gave up their lives, killing over 7,000 allied naval personnel. Our reporter Mélodie Sforza met one of the last surviving former kamikaze pilots.

stories.title: UN chief says additional $1.1 billion urgently needed to fight Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: As a fast-growing Ebola outbreak grips the Democratic Republic of Congo, the United Nations is warning of a critical funding gap. Secretary-General António Guterres says another 1.1 billion dollars is urgently needed to contain the crisis.

stories.title: Sweetener used in chewing gum and jam linked to strokes and heart attacks
stories.summary: High blood levels of xylitol associated with higher risk of major cardiovascular events, in largest study of its kind A common sweetener used in products such as chewing gum, toothpaste, jam, yoghurts and ice cream worldwide has been linked to an increased risk of strokes, heart attacks and death. Xylitol is a sugar alcohol present in some natural foods in very low amounts. It is also added – often in amounts 1,000 times higher – to artificially sweeten foods, beverages and oral care products. stories.title: Sweden to reinforce Finnish patrols along border with Russia with its own units
stories.summary: These may include Swedish JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets and Visby-class corvettes
article_sentences: The Swedish government has decided to send units to Finland to bolster its territorial defense in response to Helsinki’s request for military support, the country’s armed forces said in a press release.
"This fall, the armed forces will deploy units to bolster Finland's defenses against drones.
Currently, the armed forces are strengthening the alliance’s eastern defenses by leveraging capabilities to counter drones in the air and at sea.

In response to a request for support through joint operations, Sweden has agreed to provide Finland with military support to further strengthen its defenses against drone incursions," the statement said.

The operation to support Finland will take place this fall, during which "Swedish units may be placed under Finnish command if necessary." These may include Swedish JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets, Visby-class corvettes, as well as radar and air defense systems.
